Author: G. Radha Rani
Bench: G. Radha Rani
 The Honourable Dr.Justice G. Radha Rani
 Criminal Petition Nos.3717 and 3718 of 2024
Common Order:

These Criminal Petitions are filed by the petitioners - A1 and A2 respectively under Sections 437 and 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail in Crime No.2481 of 2023 of Cyber Crime Police Station, Hyderabad, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 66(C) and 66(D) of Information Technology Act and Sections 419 and 420 of IPC.
2.

The case of the prosecution in brief was that on 31.10.2023 at 14:30 hours, the de facto complainant lodged a report stating that on 31.08.2023, she received a message in Telegram App from @chanana425, who stated that there was a part time job and she only had to subscribe and like the YouTube Channel.
Considering it to be genuine, she asked them as to how to start to work.
They stated that she had to register in the given link of mega pro digital marketing group.
From there, she would get the work.
By following the instructions, she got registered in the said link.
They had given her few channels to like and subscribe and after that to share a screen shot to them.
She blindly followed them and did the same.
Initially, they sent Rs.50/-.
Later, they stated that she should invest and could earn huge amount from it.
She started sharing them Dr.GRR, J crlp_3717 & 3718_2024 amount.
Initially, she paid an amount of Rs.8,500/- and they refunded her Rs.10,925/-.
Convinced by such payments, she paid a total amount of Rs.40,49,900/-.
On 21.10.2023, she received a message in Telegram App from @Singh_5128, who stated that there was a part time job and she had to like the Instagram reels.
She blindly followed them and did the same.
Initially, they sent Rs.150/-.
Later they stated that, she should invest and could earn huge amount from it.

Believing the same,
she started sharing the amount.
She shared an amount of Rs.96,000/-.
But nothing was refunded.
She lost an amount of Rs.8,96,000/-, in total, she lost an amount of Rs.49,45,900/-.
3. Basing on the said report, the above crime was registered against unknown offenders.

4. Subsequently, the Inspector of Police of Cyber Crime Police Station, Detective Department,
Hyderabad sought for the details of the fraud transactions in account numbers pertaining to the victim and obtained reply from the concerned banks, wherein they furnished the beneficiary account details into which accounts, the victim transferred the amounts.

sentences.text: As per the tower location of the said number, they found the said address located at Sowhirda Nagar - 136, Leksham Veedu, Kavanad P.O., Kollam, Kerala State.

During the course of investigation, they also found that the mobile number 6282883612, which was used in the commission of offence had been inserted in IMEI numbers, was found to be roaming in Kerala.

Upon verifying the Gmail details and analyzing the call detail records, it was found that the accused person was operating from Palaniyarpalayam, Pazhaniyarpalayam, Kozhinjampara, Palakkad of Kerala State.

After obtaining permission from the superiors, the Investigating Officer proceeded to Kerala and basing on the tower locations of the mobile numbers, apprehended the accused persons A1 and A2 near Raviraj Theater in Kozhinjampara and arrested them on 21.02.2024.
He recorded their confession cum seizure panchanamas, seized the incriminating material, brought them to Hyderabad and produced them before the Court.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners had not committed any offences as alleged.
Their involvement in the said crime was not based on any admissible evidence on record.

Though all the offences alleged against the petitioners were punishable with imprisonment for less than seven Dr.GRR, J crlp_3717 & 3718_2024 years, no notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. was issued to the petitioners and they were arrested in violation of the mandatory procedure under Section 41-A Cr.P.C.

They were entitled to be released on bail, if the mandatory procedure under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. was not complied, by virtue of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another 1.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners were implicated in the above case only by filament of their imagination without any legal basis and prayed to enlarge the petitioners on bail.

7. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed grant of bail to the petitioners stating that as per the confession of the petitioner - A1, he used to do P2P trading in binance for side income along with his childhood friend by name Manual (the petitioner - A2 herein) and one Abinu (shown as absconding).

In that process, he was introduced to a person in Telegram App by name Raisul Islam,
R/o. Dubai, native of Nagapattnam, Tamilnadu State.
Raisul stated that he would send daily 3000 USDT to 4000 USDT to his binance wallet.
For that deal, in the month of August, 2023, he along with his friends Manual and Abinu visited Dubai to meet Raisul Islam.
Raisul offered him to give big commission, if he would hand over the said money to his associates in Indian Rupees.
Later, they came to India and opened two joint current bank accounts in ICICI Bank and Axis Bank in the name of M/s.COSOS Technologies Private Limited (2022) 10 SCC 51 Dr.GRR, J crlp_3717 & 3718_2024
(Proprietors: Johnny and Abinu)
After opening the bank account, they started doing business deal with Raisul Islam by taking 3% commission.
Then, Raisul Islam created a Whatsapp group namely 'Traders'.
They were the group members in that group.
After Raisul Islam sent the USDT to their binance wallet and post those screen shots in Whatsapp group, then they would sell those USDT to others for good profits.
After selling those USDT then they would receive money in Indian Rupees.

After that Raisul Islam would give his associate bank account numbers and then they would transfer that money to those bank accounts by keeping 3% commission and later used to share the commission amount among each other.

sentences.text: He further contended that the petitioners were doing online fraud and were cheating the victims in an organized manner.
To verify the money trail and to verify the bank passbooks, cheque books and debit cards, their presence was required.
As such, they were arrested and prayed to dismiss the bail application of the petitioners.

9. Perused the record and the remand report of the petitioners herein.
10.

As seen from the remand report of petitioners herein, the Investigating Officer had obtained the details of the beneficiary account details into whose accounts the victim's amount were transferred and also obtained a second layer account number, into which the said amounts were transferred and traced out its Dr.GRR, J crlp_3717 & 3718_2024 origin to one M/s.COSOS Technologies Private Limited, for which the petitioner - A1 was one of the proprietors.
He also obtained the details of the mobile number and the Gmail ID, for which the SMS alerts would be sent by the Bank Authorities.
Basing on the tower location of the said mobile numbers, apprehended A1 and A2 from a place at Kerala.
11. Thus, the investigation conducted by the Investigating Agency prima facie pointed a finger of suspicion to the involvement of the petitioners herein.
It was for the petitioners to explain as to how they were receiving the said amounts.

A1 in his confession stated about his business dealings with one Raisul Islam, resident of Dubai that Raisul Islam would be sending USDT to a binance wallet and after selling those USDT, they would receive money in Indian Rupees and were transferring money to the bank accounts of the associates of Raisul Islam by keeping their 3% commission,
which would not satisfactorily explain their business dealings.

As the said Raisul Islam was shown as absconding and his role also needs to be investigated and if the petitioners were released, they might cause disappearance of evidence or tampering with the evidence, it is considered not a fit case to release the petitioners on bail at this stage.

12. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners with regard to non-compliance of the notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. is considered not fatal, Dr.GRR, J crlp_3717 & 3718_2024 as the Investigating Officer himself explained the reasons that necessitated the arrest of the petitioners in their remand report.

As the Investigating Officer could satisfactorily explain the reasons as to why the arrest of the petitioners was required and considering that this is a case of online fraud, where the victims were cheated in an organized manner and to verify the money trail and to know the details of the other persons involved and for proper investigation of the case, their arrest was required, this Court does not find merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners on this aspect.

13. Considering the complicated nature of fraud involved in these types of cases and a variety of financial transactions to launder the amounts received and the accused persons were also belonging to various States and Countries and as it is also not easy to trace out the money trail, it is considered not fit to release the petitioners on bail at this stage.
14. In the result, the Criminal Petitions are dismissed.
